reference_opening.argument: This video is scam content because it promotes CloudToken by presenting claimed Bitcoin trading and passive-income returns, including approximately 25.104 Bitcoin being traded and recurring income. It invites viewers to join, use a link, take action, or contact the person who shared the video while claiming the opportunity could make viewers millions. A sampled Cloud Token screen displays a “Phishing site reported” warning, but the material does not establish who issued it, whether it is accurate or current, or whether anyone transferred funds or suffered a loss.

citations.quote: I have 25 thousand plus tokens on my own account, it's been 20 days now. I am now trading 20 Bitcoin. So you have to click on projects, click on the Jawisai and you can see I have 25.104 Bitcoin trading for me returning approximately 0.3 per day for around about 10 passive income per month
With CloudToken, it shows you your order history in your application live
it's a matter of just taking action
any questions get back to the person who shared this video with you
going to help you make millions of dollars with this incredible opportunity

opening.argument: The presentation uses qualified, approximate language rather than certifying a guaranteed result. The description says the program is something “that we believe can go for long time,” while the speaker describes returns as “approximately” and “around about,” signaling personal expectation and estimation. The material therefore reads as an enthusiastic opinion about a volatile opportunity, not a promise that every viewer will profit. The cited recommendation may be strong, but a recommendation is not itself proof of deception, especially where the claims are expressly framed as belief and approximation.

citations.quote: that we believe can go for long time
returning approximately 0.3 per day for around about 10 passive income per month
it gets my top recommendation guys

rebuttal.rebuttal: The reference side treats enthusiastic language as if it removes all qualification. But “approximately” and “around about” are not guarantees, and the description expressly limits the longevity claim to what the speaker believes. The fact that the speaker invites action does not establish that the opportunity is deceptive; it is consistent with an opinionated recommendation accompanied by uncertainty.

citations.quote: that we believe can go for long time
returning approximately 0.3 per day for around about 10 passive income per month

true_side_reply.rebuttal: Approximate wording does not neutralize the overall solicitation. The speaker pairs estimated returns with a specific account claim and calls the opportunity his top recommendation, then says it will help viewers make millions. Calling a claim an estimate or belief does not provide a meaningful risk warning or independent support for the advertised outcome.

citations.quote: I have 25 thousand plus tokens on my own account, it's been 20 days now. I am now trading 20 Bitcoin
going to help you make millions of dollars with this incredible opportunity

opening.argument: The core activity shown is an operational walkthrough of an application. The speaker explains how to reach “order history,” describes the display as pulling information live from an exchange, and the sampled frames visibly show the application's order-history screen and project-management screens. That is consistent with demonstrating how the interface works and where its records appear. Showing a personal use case and explaining navigation is not the same as certifying that a viewer will obtain the same result; the video can be understood as commentary and a product demonstration.

citations.quote: all you do is you click on three bars at the top and then order history
this is pulling the information live off the exchange

rebuttal.rebuttal: The reference side emphasizes promotional phrases while overlooking the video's concrete instructional structure: it explains the menu path and shows the relevant application screens. The order-history display is evidence of what the interface presents, not automatically evidence that the creator is making a deceptive claim. A demonstration can include a favorable personal assessment without becoming a scam solicitation.

citations.quote: all you do is you click on three bars at the top and then order history

true_side_reply.rebuttal: The walkthrough is not neutral technical education. The interface instructions are used to support claims of trading performance and recurring passive income, and the speaker concludes with an invitation to act and a promise of millions. A screen showing order history demonstrates only that entries are displayed; it does not verify trading, profits, or the promised outcome.

citations.quote: With CloudToken, it shows you your order history in your application live
returning approximately 0.3 per day for around about 10 passive income per month
going to help you make millions of dollars with this incredible opportunity

opening.argument: At most, this is promotion of access to a cryptocurrency application and an associated service. The supplied material does not show a request for a deposit, credentials, a downline, or payment from the viewer. Nor do the sampled screens establish that anyone transferred funds or suffered a loss; they show application panels and order-history entries. The speaker even says the Bitcoin remains owned by the user and can be withdrawn or sold. Those facts support treating this as ordinary service promotion, while the missing scam mechanism makes a non-scam classification more appropriate.

citations.quote: you still own your bitcoin so all that bitcoin is still yours
you can withdraw it and you can use it and sell it and do what you like with it

rebuttal.rebuttal: The reference side identifies promotion and claimed returns, but those features can occur in ordinary financial-service promotion. Its cited invitation to contact a sharer does not itself show a payment demand, credential request, or recruitment structure. The available screens likewise do not establish a loss or a transfer. Without a demonstrated mechanism beyond favorable claims about a service, the evidence remains insufficient to call the promotion a scam.

citations.quote: any questions get back to the person who shared this video with you
you still own your bitcoin so all that bitcoin is still yours

true_side_reply.rebuttal: A scam classification does not require the video to document a completed loss or display a credential request. The relevant conduct is promoting a service through claimed Bitcoin trading, recurring passive income, and an instruction to take action. The statement that Bitcoin remains yours is itself an unverified assurance, while the application screens do not independently establish the claimed trading or returns.
